papers.title: Selective Laser Melting of Graphene-Reinforced Inconel 718 Superalloy: Evaluation of Microstructure and Tensile Performance
papers.abstract: Graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) have many outstanding properties, such as high mechanical strengths, light weight, and high electric conductivity. These unique properties make it an ideal reinforcement used for metal matrix composites (MMCs). In the past few years, many studies have been performed to incorporate GNPs into metal matrix and investigate the properties of obtained metal matrix composites. Meanwhile, fabrication of MMCs through laser-assisted additive manufacturing (LAAM) has attracted much attention in recent years due to the advantages of low waste, high precision, short production lead time, and high workpiece complexity capability. In this study, the two attractive features are combined to produce GNPs reinforced MMC using selective laser melting (SLM) process, one of the LAAM processes. The target metal matrix material is Inconel 718, a nickel-based Ni–Cr–Fe austenitic superalloy that possesses excellent workability and mechanical performance, and has wide applications in industries. In the experiment, pure Inconel 718 and GNPs reinforced Inconel 718 composites with two levels of GNPs content (i.e., 0.25 and 1 wt. %) are obtained by SLM. Note that before the SLM process, a novel powder mixture procedure is employed to ensure the even dispersion of GNPs in the Inconel 718 powders. Room temperature tensile tests are conducted to evaluate the tensile properties. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations are conducted to analyze the fracture surface of materials and to understand the reinforcing mechanism. It is found that fabrication of GNPs reinforced MMC using SLM is a viable approach. The obtained composite possesses dense microstructure and significantly enhanced tensile strength. The ultimate tensile strengths (UTSs) are 997.8, 1296.3, and 1511.6 MPa, and the Young's moduli are 475, 536, and 675 GPa, for 0 wt. % (pure Inconel 718), 0.25 wt. %, and 1 wt. % GNP additions, respectively. The bonding between GNPs and matrix material appears to be strong, and GNPs could be retained during the SLM process. The strengthening effect and mechanisms involved in the composites are discussed. Load transfer, thermal expansion coefficient mismatch, and dislocation hindering are believed to be the three main reinforcing mechanisms involved. It should be noted that more work needs to be conducted in the future to obtain more comprehensive information regarding other static and dynamic properties and the high-temperature performances of the GNP-reinforced MMCs produced by SLM. Process parameter optimization should also be investigated.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究工业用镍基高温合金的激光选区熔化，不涉及生物医学植入物或应力遮挡问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on SLM of graphene-reinforced Inconel 718 for industrial applications, with no biomedical context, no porous structure, no stress shielding analysis, no fatigue testing, and no surface roughness or osseointegration evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用石墨烯增强金属基复合材料并探索SLM可行性。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM制备不同石墨烯含量的Inconel 718复合材料并测试拉伸性能。
summary_zh.result: 复合材料致密，拉伸强度显著提升，最高达1511.6 MPa。
summary_zh.validation: 通过SEM和室温拉伸测试验证微观结构和力学性能。

summary_en.motivation: To combine graphene nanoplatelets with a nickel superalloy via selective laser melting for enhanced mechanical performance.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was used to fabricate Inconel 718 composites with 0, 0.25, and 1 wt% graphene nanoplatelets, followed by room-temperature tensile tests and SEM fractography.
summary_en.result: The composites achieved fully dense microstructures and significant improvements in ultimate tensile strength (up to 1511.6 MPa) and Young's modulus (up to 675 GPa) with increasing graphene content.
summary_en.validation: Tensile testing and SEM analysis confirmed the strengthening effects and strong graphene-matrix bonding.

papers.title: Fatigue crack growth threshold of Selective Laser Melted Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) of Ti-6Al-4V has gained interest in industry over recent years due to its ability to produce geometrically complex components for engineering applications. In order for important industries such as aerospace and biomedical to accept SLM Ti-6Al-4V for their applications, there needs to be a great understanding of the SLM technology. Previous work has shown that there’s in an intricate link between porosity, residual stress and microstructure which affects the mechanical properties of SLM Ti-6Al-4V. These intricacies have also shown to be dependent on specific SLM processes such as scan parameters and scan strategies, amongst others. The interest then lies in establishing this link, specifically focussing on fatigue threshold and crack initiation characteristics, in order to obtain a true understanding of the properties in relation to the specific SLM process.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了选区激光熔化Ti-6Al-4V的疲劳裂纹扩展阈值，对理解植入物材料的疲劳性能有参考价值。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address porous structures, stress shielding, or osseointegration, and lacks direct application to hip implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 理解SLM Ti-6Al-4V的疲劳裂纹扩展门槛，推动其在航空和生物医学中的应用。
summary_zh.method: 实验研究孔隙率、残余应力和微观结构对疲劳性能的影响。
summary_zh.result: 建立了SLM工艺参数与疲劳裂纹萌生及门槛之间的联系。
summary_zh.validation: 通过机械疲劳测试验证。

summary_en.motivation: To understand the fatigue crack growth threshold of SLM Ti-6Al-4V to enable its use in critical aerospace and biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Experimental investigation correlating porosity, residual stress, and microstructure with fatigue crack initiation and threshold behavior.
summary_en.result: Established a clear link between SLM process parameters (scan strategies, parameters) and fatigue crack growth resistance.
summary_en.validation: Validation via mechanical fatigue testing on SLM-produced Ti-6Al-4V specimens.

papers.title: INVESTIGATING ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY FOR APPLICATION IN THE AEROSPACE INDUSTRY
papers.abstract: INVESTIGATING ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY FOR APPLICATION IN THE AEROSPACE INDUSTRY W.M. Makhetha [1] * & T.Becker [2] 1 Department of Industrial Engineering University of Stellenbosch, South Africa makhetham@cput.ac.za 2 Department of Industrial Engineering University of Stellenbosch, South Africa tbecker@sun.ac.za ABSTRACT Although Additive Manufacturing (AM) technology has undergone significant development in the recent year, it is still not widely accepted by most industries [1]. By gaining a true understanding of the link between production and part structural integrity, we can significantly increase the readiness of the technology; hence the following research will be contributing towards the readiness of the technology for application in the aerospace industry. Keywords : Selective Laser Melting, Titanium Alloys. 1.          INTRODUCTION Additive Manufacturing (AM) processes make three-dimensional parts directly from CAD models by adding materials layer by layer [1], offering the beneficial ability to build parts with geometric and material complexities that could not be produced by subtractive manufacturing processes. AM technology includes Selective Laser Melting (SLM), Selective Laser Sintering (SLS), 3 Dimensional Printing (3DP) and Electron Beam Melting (EBM). The research will focus on SLM of titanium alloys. 2.       LITERATURE REVIEW The SLM technology, is known to allow the production of parts in a wide range of metallic materials by selectively fusing a metallic powder material without bonding agents [2]. Choosing appropriate processing parameters when using this technology allows the part-porosity to be kept below 1%; hence important if dense parts are desired [3]. The ability of this technology to reduce porosity therefore results in mechanical properties being widely comparable to those obtained from conventionally processed materials. For the technology to be widely accepted by industries, the repeatability and consistency of the manufactured parts are critical [1]. What makes investigations intricate is that the material performance, in for example SLM, depends on numerous factors including material powder characteristics, process parameters and post-processing procedures to name a few. 3.       CONCLUSION The inherent nature of AM, i.e. fast production, makes post-processing undesirable; hence the focus of this research on process parameters and post-processing procedures as these have a significant impact on the part’s structural integrity. Therefore, by gaining a true understanding of the link between production and part structural integrity for specific AM parts significantly increases the readiness of the technology. Osakada, K. Nakamura, T. Yamashita, and F. Abe, “Residual Stress within Metallic Model Made by Selective Laser Melting Process,” CIRP Ann. - Manuf. Technol. , vol. 53, no. 1, pp. 195–198, 2004. [3]       A. B. Spierings, K. Wegener, and G. papers.title: In vitro and in vivo study of additive manufactured porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds for repairing bone defects.
papers.abstract: Metallic implants with a low effective modulus can provide early load-bearing and reduce stress shielding, which is favorable for increasing in vivo life-span. In this research, porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds with three pore sizes (300~400, 400~500, and 500~700 μm) were manufactured by Electron Beam Melting, with an elastic modulus range of 3.7 to 1.7 GPa. Cytocompatibility in vitro and osseointegration ability in vivo of scaffolds were assessed. hBMSCs numbers increased on all porous scaffolds over time. The group with intended pore sizes of 300 to 400 μm was significantly higher than that of the other two porous scaffolds at days 5 and 7. This group also had higher ALP activity at day 7 in osteogenic differentiation experiment. The scaffold with pore size of 300 to 400 μm was implanted into a 30-mm segmental defect of goat metatarsus. In vivo evaluations indicated that the depth of bone ingrowth increased over time and no implant dislocation occurred during the experiment. Based on its better cytocompatibility and favorable bone ingrowth, the present data showed the capability of the additive manufactured porous Ti6Al4V scaffold with an intended pore size of 300 to 400 μm for large segmental bone defects.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文通过EBM制造多孔Ti6Al4V支架，研究孔径对应力遮挡和骨整合的影响，与用户关注的AM生物医用材料方向直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: Uses Electron Beam Melting instead of LPBF, no fatigue testing, no surface roughness characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 降低弹性模量以减少应力遮挡，延长植入体寿命。
summary_zh.method: 采用电子束熔融制造三种孔径的多孔Ti6Al4V支架，测试弹性模量并评估体外细胞相容性和体内骨整合。
summary_zh.result: 300-400 μm孔径支架在细胞增殖和碱性磷酸酶活性方面表现最佳，体内骨长入良好。
summary_zh.validation: 通过山羊跖骨节段性骨缺损模型进行体内验证。

summary_en.motivation: Metallic implants with low effective modulus can reduce stress shielding and improve lifespan; this study evaluates porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds with varying pore sizes.
summary_en.method: Porous Ti6Al4V scaffolds with three pore size ranges (300-400, 400-500, 500-700 μm) were fabricated by Electron Beam Melting, and their mechanical properties, in vitro cytocompatibility, and in vivo osseointegration were assessed.
summary_en.result: Scaffolds with 300-400 μm pores showed significantly higher cell proliferation and alkaline phosphatase activity, and successful bone ingrowth in a goat segmental defect model.
summary_en.validation: Validation included in vitro cell assays (hBMSCs, ALP) and in vivo implantation in a goat metatarsal defect with histological analysis.
